ve the composer, and send them to the agent.
# Annotations — a DSH client plugin
Select text in a DeepSeek Harness reply or in a document previewed in the right sidebar; a comment b
ox appears. `Enter` confirms the annotation and collects it into an aggregated "N notes" card above
the composer; `Cmd/Ctrl+Enter` sends every pending annotation to the AI in one message.

## Usage
| Action | Result |

| Select text | The comment box appears next to the selection and gets focus |
| Type + `Enter` | Co

nfirms the annotation; it is collected into the "N notes" card above the composer |
| `Cmd/Ctrl + En
ter` | Confirms and immediately sends **all pending** annotations to the AI (works inside the commen

t box or while no input is focused) |
| `Shift + Enter` | Newline inside the comment |
| `Cmd/Ctrl +
C` with no text selected in the comment box | Copies the passage that opened the box (focusing the

box collapses the document selection) |
| `Esc` | Cancels the comment box |
| Click the "N notes" ca

rd | Expands the quotes and notes; jump to or delete each one |
| Send with text already in the comp
oser | The typed message and all pending annotations go to the AI as one message (attachments preser

ved) |
| Click a numbered dot / highlighted text | Edit or delete that annotation; the number matche

s its row in the list |
| Sidebar footer → Annotations | Opens the annotation list as a native **rig
ht-sidebar tab** (conversation / documents / other documents), beside the chat instead of over it; j
* (conversation / documents / other documents), beside the chat instead of over it; jump or delete |
The message the AI receives looks like this:

The message language follows the current DSH UI language.
## Where it works, and the limits
| Surface | Supported |

| Assistant reply body in the conversation | Yes (including expanded reasoning) |
| Markdown / plain

text / code previews in the right sidebar | Yes |
| PDF and Word/PowerPoint-to-PDF text layers in t

he right sidebar | Yes, where text is selectable |
| Excel preview in the right sidebar | No — the g

rid is not document text |
| HTML / web page previews in the right sidebar | No — the body runs in a

n opaque-origin iframe, so the parent page cannot read its selection |
| Images, terminal | No |
These limits come from how the host renders those surfaces, not from the plugin.
## Design choices

- **One highlight color.** The comments carry the emphasis, so there is no color picker.
- **Compose
r stays clean.** Annotations are not pasted into the input as text; they aggregate into one "N notes

" card that expands on click.
- **Sidebar list stays.** Open it from the sidebar footer; it docks as

a native right-sidebar tab next to documents instead of covering the conversation.
- **No export, c
opy, or diagnostics extras.** The plugin only annotates and sends.
## Annotation lifecycle
- Annotations live in `localStorage`; the list only shows **chat annotations of the active session p

lus document annotations**.
- **Deleted session** — its chat annotations are pruned automatically af
ter startup or when the list is opened. The automatic pass only runs once the session index is stabl

e across two counts, so a partially loaded sidebar is never mistaken for deleted sessions.
- **Archi
ved session** — its annotations are kept because the session can be reopened. They do not count towa

rd the active session badge; use "Clean up → Clean other sessions" to remove them.
- **Document anno
tations** — removed about a second after the batch is sent, and stale sent document annotations are

pruned on load, so PDF highlights do not survive into a later modification round.
- **Conversation a
nnotations** — sent highlights and list rows stay until you choose "Clean up → Clean sent annotation

s".
- **Document annotations** — tied to the file path and never auto-pruned; delete them row by row
ument annotations** — tied to the file path and never auto-pruned; delete them row by row if needed.
## How it works
- **Client-only bundle.** `index.js` exports an empty `apply()`; all behavior lives in `client.js`.

- **Additive slots only** — no shipped UI is replaced:
- `shell.overlay` — comment box, highlight do

t, edit dialog, annotation list, toasts;
- `conversation.input.overlay` — the aggregated card above

the composer;
- `sidebar.right.pane.tab` — the annotation list as a right-sidebar tab (registered th

rough `sidebarRightTabs` as the `annotation` kind);
- `sidebar.footer.action` — the Annotations entr

y at the sidebar foot, opening or focusing that tab.
- **Highlights use the CSS Custom Highlight API
** (`::highlight()` + `CSS.highlights`), so React-owned text is never mutated and streaming/folding

cannot conflict.
- **Quote anchoring** — each segment stores `exact/prefix/suffix/start`; re-renders
resolve it with context scoring. Chat rows are addressed by `data-chat-anchor-key` inside `[data-co

nversation-session]`; sidebar documents by `data-textpreview-url` / resource address.
- **Sending**

uses `sessions.scope(sessionId).conversation.send(text)` to deliver the batch as one user message.
-
**Numbering** — current-session chat annotations plus document annotations are numbered 1..N in cre

ation order; dots, the composer card and the sidebar list share that numbering.
- **Persistence** in
`localStorage` under `dsh.annotation.v1` (per browser profile, synced across windows via `storage`
torage` under `dsh.annotation.v1` (per browser profile, synced across windows via `storage` events).
## Install
Install from npm:

Or ask the DSH agent to install the checkout with `plugin_manager` `install_bundle`, then refresh th
SH agent to install the checkout with `plugin_manager` `install_bundle`, then refresh the page once.
Uninstall through Plugin Manager; annotations stay in `localStorage`.
## Development
[代码示例省略，未执行]
No dependencies beyond Node.js built-ins.
## Known limits

- Annotations live in the current browser profile only.
- PDF support covers selectable text layers;

scanned image-only PDFs cannot be annotated.
- Changes to `client.js` need a page refresh.
- If a t
hird-party sidebar renders its own button over the selection, the comment box tries to avoid it.
